investigator.method: A targeted re-investigation, explicitly authorised, of the ONE open question the superseded teatro-sao-luiz-lisbon-01 investigation deliberately left to a human/operator decision: whether a policy-compliant (v1.2) DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT derivation can establish the full-season calendar year for every event, not just the 6 months -01 happened to sample. Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC (INSUFFICIENT for this specific question) then Level 2 STRUCTURAL (SUFFICIENT). All retained evidence freshly re-acquired via plain curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion) on 2026-08-27, two days after -01. Level 1: re-fetched the EN+PT programme pages, EN+PT home pages, the PT+EN 'Temporadas Anteriores'/'Seasons' archive pages, and the box-office ('Bilheteira') page, searching all of them for any first-party PROSE sentence stating the season's own month boundaries -- none was found (the season is only ever labelled '2026-2027', never spelled out as 'runs from month X to month Y' in plain text). The box-office page's own operating-hours text ('a partir de 1 de setembro' / 'entre 1 a 31 de agosto') was retained as corroborating (but not yet sufficient on its own, being about box-office hours rather than an explicit season/year rule) first-party context. This confirmed Level 1 alone still could not answer the specific question this investigation exists to resolve, justifying escalation. Level 2: inspected the site's own public theme JavaScript bundle (wp-content/themes/tsl/js/main.js, referenced directly by the retained programme page's own <script> tag -- public bootstrap/client code, not a private/undocumented asset) and found a literal, unconditional, non-time-dependent comparison hardcoded in the site's own season-selector change handler: a month number 8-12 maps to the season label's own start-year component, and (via the same code's else branch) a month number 1-7 maps to the season label's own end-year component. This rule was then independently, empirically re-confirmed by re-querying the same auxiliary /wp-json/custom/v1/espetaculos endpoint -01 had already discovered, but this time for literal EVERY month of the season (01 through 12, not the 6 -01 sampled) -- 46 real, year-inclusive date entries were returned across 9 non-empty months, and every single one matched the JS rule's predicted year for its own month, with zero contradictions. A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script re-parsed every retained fixture to mechanically reproduce this finding, apply the proven rule to all 26 events on the freshly re-fetched static programme list, and independently re-confirm the WordPress shortlink source_record_id's stability (including across the two investigations, days apart). Level 2 was SUFFICIENT; no browser/headless session (Level 3) was opened.

probe_history.reason: Plain curl GETs (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) of https://www.teatrosaoluiz.pt/en/programme/, /programacao/, /en/, /, /temporadas/, /en/seasons/, and /bilheteira/ all returned 200 OK. All of them state the season label '2026-2027' repeatedly (a <body data-temporada-actual> attribute, a <select> option, a breadcrumb span, an <aside data-season> attribute) but NONE of them contains a plain-text sentence stating which calendar months belong to which half of the season (mechanically confirmed: evidence/offline-proof.mjs Step 2 greps every retained static page for a 'decorre de setembro a ... julho/agosto' -style sentence and finds none). The box-office page does independently state its own opening hours run 'a partir de 1 de setembro' (from 1 September) and that it closes 'entre 1 a 31 de agosto' (1-31 August) -- real, retained, first-party corroboration that the venue's own operating year turns over at the Aug/Sep boundary -- but this is a statement about box-office hours, not an explicit, general season/year mapping rule an investigator could mechanically apply to every event without further work. A GET-parameter probe of the 'Temporadas Anteriores' (previous seasons) archive filter (?opt_filter=2025-2026) was also tried, in case an archived, already-completed season's own event list would show real historical full dates as a second empirical check -- it returned the same static 'no results' shell as an unfiltered request, confirming that filter is AJAX-driven (via admin-ajax.php, not fetched further) rather than server-rendered, so it could not be used as a plain static data path. Level 1 alone therefore cannot establish an explicit, mechanical season-boundary rule -- only Level 2 (public JS/bootstrap inspection) could locate the site's own client-side rule, so escalation was justified.

Inspecting the same public programme page's own referenced theme JavaScript asset (wp-content/themes/tsl/js/main.js, plus plugins.js, both fetched as plain public GETs -- per Level 2 guidance: 'inspect public JS/bootstrap data') found a literal, source-authored, non-time-dependent rule inside the season-selector's own 'change' handler: `if (currentMonth >= 8 && currentMonth <= 12) { selectedMonth = selectedSeason.split('-')[0] + '-' + currentMonth; } else { selectedMonth = selectedSeason.split('-')[1] + '-' + currentMonth; }` -- i.e. month numbers 8-12 map to the season label's own start-year component, and month numbers 1-7 map to its own end-year component, evaluated purely against literal integers, never against `new Date()` or any other real-world clock value in this branch. This rule was then independently, empirically re-confirmed (per Level 2's own 'inspect publicly-referenced endpoints' guidance) by re-querying the already-discovered /wp-json/custom/v1/espetaculos endpoint for literal EVERY month of the season (01 through 12), not merely the 6 months -01 sampled: 9 of the 12 months returned real, year-inclusive dated entries (46 entries total), and mechanically checking every single one (evidence/offline-proof.mjs Steps 5a/5b) found the returned year matched the JS rule's own prediction for that month with ZERO contradictions anywhere. Applying the proven rule to all 26 events on the freshly re-fetched static programme list (evidence/offline-proof.mjs Step 6) resolves every one of them to exactly one of the season's two calendar years, with no ambiguity. This already fully answers the one open question this investigation exists to resolve, so escalation to Level 3 (BROWSER_OBSERVATION) was not attempted.

start_date.notes: THE central finding of this v1.2 re-investigation, and the one gap that kept -01 at HUMAN_REVIEW. The retained static list gives every event's own day-of-month and month name (e.g. 'Batucadeiras das Olaias (PT)': '9 September') but never a calendar year, exactly as -01 found. This investigation establishes the year mechanically, not by assumption: the site's own public theme JavaScript (wp-content/themes/tsl/js/main.js) hardcodes an unconditional, non-time-dependent rule mapping a month number to one of the season label's own two year components (month 8-12 -> the season's start-year component; month 1-7 -> its end-year component -- see derivation below). This rule was independently, empirically re-tested against literal every month (01-12) of the season's own auxiliary calendar API (not merely the 6 months -01 sampled): 46 real, year-inclusive date entries were returned across 9 non-empty months (Feb/Mar/Aug returned no data at all -- never a conflicting year), and every single one matched the rule's own prediction for its month, with ZERO contradictions (evidence/offline-proof.mjs Steps 5a/5b). Applying the proven rule to all 26 events on the freshly re-fetched static list (Step 6c) resolves every one of them to exactly one of the season's two calendar years -- 23 events to 2026 (September/October/November/December), 3 events to 2027 (January x2, April) -- with no event falling outside the season and no ambiguity. Representative value shown ('2026-09-09') is for Batucadeiras das Olaias, the first list event; a multi-day event's OWN date range (e.g. Picadeiro Fest 2026, '9 - 13 September') resolves to a start AND end date via the identical rule, both printed per-event in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt. Today's date, agent knowledge, or a probable/likely season were never consulted anywhere in this derivation -- the rule is evaluated purely against the season label's own two integer year components and the retained JS's own literal 8/12 boundary integers.

derivation.rule: Convert the event's own month name (from the retained static programme list) to a month number 1-12. Split the site's own season label (its own 'data-temporada-actual' / 'data-season' attribute, e.g. '2026-2027') into a start-year component and an end-year component. Apply the two-branch mapping hardcoded, unconditionally, in the site's own public theme JavaScript (wp-content/themes/tsl/js/main.js): a month number in the fixed range 8-12 maps to the season label's start-year component; any other month number (1-7) maps to the season label's end-year component. This mapping does not read or depend on the real-world clock at the moment it is evaluated -- it is a fixed comparison against literal integers baked into the site's own retained source code, evaluated the same way regardless of when the derivation is run. Concatenate the mapped year with the month number and the event's own day-of-month as YYYY-MM-DD. This mapping was independently, empirically re-confirmed against every one of the season's own auxiliary calendar API's 12 months, with zero contradictions across 46 real returned date entries.
inputs: 2026-2027 (site's own season label, from data-temporada-actual / data-season attributes on the retained programme and calendar pages)

blockers.description: The season-boundary rule this investigation relies on lives only in the theme's own public main.js bundle (observed at theme asset version 'ver=7.1'). If the theme is later redesigned or this script is rewritten, the literal rule (or its exact 8/12 boundary integers) could change or be removed without notice. A future collector baking this rule in as a documented constant should periodically re-verify the retained JS still states the identical rule (e.g. by re-running a version of this investigation's offline-proof script against a freshly re-fetched main.js) rather than treating it as permanently fixed.

August (month 8) is empirically untested by this investigation's own data: the auxiliary calendar API returned zero events for month=08, and the box office's own retained closure statement covers the whole of August, consistent with there being no real event to check that month against. The rule's own boundary places August in the SAME bucket as September-December (the season's start year), which the retained evidence neither confirms nor contradicts for that specific month -- this is recorded honestly as an untested edge rather than silently assumed correct, and would need re-checking if the site is ever observed to schedule an August event.

A multi-day run (e.g. O Pai, 16-27 September; Picadeiro Fest, 9-13 September) is represented by exactly one WordPress post / one shortlink id for the whole run, with no structured per-date breakdown at all -- only a free-text date range plus, sometimes, weekday-conditional show times. A collector wanting one Observation per individual performance date, not one per run, would need its own non-source-provided convention to enumerate and key individual occurrences. Unchanged from -01.

The auxiliary /wp-json/custom/v1/espetaculos endpoint remains an unreliable, incomplete mirror of the static programme as an EVENTS feed (unchanged finding from -01 -- e.g. its own January response includes 'NA MINHA BOCA', a title absent from the retained static English programme list entirely). This investigation used it solely to falsification-test the theme-JS year-mapping rule, never as a source of event titles/venues/prices -- a future collector must not be tempted to use it as a primary or supplementary events feed on the strength of this investigation's positive year-mapping finding.
